mainTopic: Why a גט must be dated (the reasons of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש and how they fit רבי שמעון and the רבנן), and אביי's questions to רב יוסף about how the dating rule works in practice.
overview: Earlier, the גמרא gave two reasons why a גט must be dated. רבי יוחנן says the date stops a husband from covering for an unfaithful wife. ריש לקיש says it settles when the husband's rights to the פירות of her property end. The גמרא explains why each rejected the other's reason, and how each fits the dispute between רבי שמעון and the רבנן about a גט written by day and signed at night. A quoted dispute seems to give them the opposite views on the produce, and the גמרא answers by switching the names there. Then אביי asks רב יוסף a series of questions about the dating rule. An undated גט works after the fact, but she may not remarry with it from the start. We do not worry about a cheater who cuts off the date. Even a general date, like a seven-year cycle, is valid because it settles what happened before and after that span. At the end רבינא begins a new question to רבא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why ריש לקיש rejects רבי יוחנן's reason
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש did not use רבי יוחנן's reason because זנות is uncommon, and the חכמים would not make a rule for an uncommon problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: Adultery is not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering an earlier question: why didn't ריש לקיש give the same reason as רבי יוחנן? The answer is that זנות is not common.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the date is there to stop a husband from protecting his unfaithful wife. ריש לקיש holds that this case is too rare for the חכמים to build a תקנה around it. So he needed a reason that applies often, which is the issue of פירות.

keyTerms.meaning: Adultery or infidelity
Not common; does not happen often
The אמורא who explains the date in a גט as being about the produce

phrases.english: Adultery is not common.

steps.triggerLanguage: זְנוּת לָא שְׁכִיחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from just before this section about why ריש לקיש did not accept רבי יוחנן's reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: זנות is rare, so the חכמים would not set up the dating rule just to deal with it.

steps.title: Why רבי יוחנן rejects ריש לקיש's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks the opposite question: why didn't רבי יוחנן use ריש לקיש's reason about the produce?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן: what is the reason he did not say like ריש לקיש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question around and asks why רבי יוחנן did not accept ריש לקיש's reason. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's reason about פירות seems practical and common. So the גמרא wants to know what problem רבי יוחנן saw with it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
The אמורא who explains the date as protection against hidden זנות

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan, what is the reason
that he did not say like Reish Lakish?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 1, now asking about the other אמורא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יוחנן did not accept the פירות reason.

steps.title: The husband keeps the produce until the גט is given
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds that the husband keeps the rights to the פירות until the גט is actually handed over, so the written date does not help with the produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: the husband has the produce until the time of giving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן holds the husband keeps the produce until the moment the גט is given. Because of this, the date written in the גט does not settle the produce question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rights to the פירות end at the time of giving, then the date of writing does not matter for them. The woman would need proof of when she received the גט. So ריש לקיש's reason does not work for רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds; his view is
Produce from the wife's property, which the husband eats during the marriage
The time the גט is given to the wife

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up writing and giving. ריש לקיש's reason works only if her rights start at the writing. רבי יוחנן says they start at the giving, which is not recorded in the גט.

phrases.english: He holds: the husband has the produce
until the time of giving.
phrases.notes: Meaning the moment the גט is handed to her, not the day it was written.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר: יֵשׁ לְבַעַל פֵּירוֹת עַד שְׁעַת נְתִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי יוחנן the husband's rights to the פירות last until the giving, so the date of writing does not help with the produce.
steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש says the date is for the פירות. רבי יוחנן says the husband keeps the פירות until the גט is given, so for him the date must be for something else.

steps.title: How does רבי יוחנן explain רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש can easily explain why רבי שמעון validates a גט signed later than it was written. But according to רבי יוחנן's reason, why would רבי שמעון validate it?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for ריש לקיש: that is why רבי שמעון validates. But for רבי יוחנן, what is רבי שמעון's reason for validating?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן using רבי שמעון from the משנה, who validates a גט written by day and signed at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, the woman gets the פירות from the time of writing, so the written date is correct even if the signing came later. For רבי יוחנן, a date earlier than the signing could let the husband cover for his wife, so why would רבי שמעון allow it?

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense for one side, but...; opens a contrast
Rules it valid
But; introduces the difficult side
The תנא in the משנה who validates the גט

phrases.english: It works well for Reish Lakish:

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם הָכִי קָא מַכְשַׁיר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.english: that is why Rabbi Shimon rules it valid.
phrases.notes: This refers to the משנה's case of a גט written by day and signed at night.

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Yochanan,
what is Rabbi Shimon's reason for ruling it valid?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, מִשּׁוּם הָכִי קָא מַכְשַׁיר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests both reasons against רבי שמעון's ruling in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reason for dating a גט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the date is meant to stop a husband from covering for his wife, a date earlier than the signing should be a problem. Yet רבי שמעון allows it.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן explains the רבנן, not רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that his reason is not meant to explain רבי שמעון. It explains the רבנן, who invalidate such a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן could say to you: I am not speaking according to רבי שמעון; when I speak, it is according to the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יוחנן: his reason was never meant to match רבי שמעון's view, only the view of the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון is simply not worried about a husband covering for his wife, so רבי יוחנן's reason does not apply to him. The רבנן invalidate the late-signed גט, and that fits רבי יוחנן's reason well.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you; introduces a defense on someone's behalf
According to the opinion of
The majority Sages; here, the first opinion in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's reason (preventing a husband from covering for זנות) explains the רבנן, who invalidate the late-signed גט. ריש לקיש's reason (פירות) can explain רבי שמעון, who validates it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan could say to you:
I am not speaking according to Rabbi Shimon;
when I speak, it is according to the Rabbanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לָא קָאָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits רבי יוחנן's reason to one side of the dispute in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed רבי יוחנן's reason had to fit every opinion in the משנה, including רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן's reason only explains the רבנן. רבי שמעון does not share his concern.

steps.title: According to ריש לקיש, what do רבי שמעון and the רבנן argue about?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's reason gives רבי שמעון and the רבנן something real to disagree about. But according to ריש לקיש's reason, both sides seem to agree, so where is their dispute?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רבי יוחנן: that is the difference between רבי שמעון and the רבנן. But according to ריש לקיש, what is the difference between רבי שמעון and the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to ריש לקיש and asks what point רבי שמעון and the רבנן could still be arguing about according to his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, רבי יוחנן explained that his reason belongs to the רבנן, who invalidate a גט signed later than it was written. רבי שמעון disagrees, so they clearly argue. ריש לקיש's produce reason seemed to fit רבי שמעון easily (step 4), so it looks like the רבנן would have nothing left to argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for / granted (one side is fine, but there is a problem with the other)
The Sages, the majority opinion that disagrees with רבי שמעון
What is the difference between (what do they actually argue about?)

phrases.english: It works well according to רבי יוחנן,

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ דְּאִיכָּא בֵּין רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְרַבָּנַן;
phrases.english: this is the difference between רבי שמעון and the רבנן;
phrases.notes: This points back to step 5: the רבנן invalidate the late-signed גט because of רבי יוחנן's reason, and רבי שמעון does not.

phrases.english: but according to ריש לקיש,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְרַבָּנַן?
phrases.english: what difference is there between רבי שמעון and the רבנן?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הַיְינוּ דְּאִיכָּא בֵּין רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְרַבָּנַן אֶלָּא לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the challenge from step 4 around: now that רבי יוחנן has a clear dispute, the גמרא checks whether ריש לקיש has one too.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's produce reason for dating a גט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ריש לקיש's reason fits רבי שמעון's lenient ruling, the רבנן seem to have no grounds to disagree, so the dispute between them disappears.

steps.title: They argue about the produce between the writing and the signing
steps.stepSummary: Even according to ריש לקיש, רבי שמעון and the רבנן argue about who gets the produce from the time the גט is written until it is signed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The produce from the time of writing until the time of signing is the difference between them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון and the רבנן argue about one specific stretch of time: from when the גט is written until it is signed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רבנן, the wife gets her rights to the produce back only once the גט is signed, so the date must match the signing. According to רבי שמעון, her rights begin when the גט is written, so a date from the day of writing is fine. That gives them a real dispute even according to ריש לקיש's reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce (the profits from the wife's property, which the husband enjoys during the marriage)
The time the גט is written
The time the witnesses sign the גט

phrases.english: The produce from the time of writing
until the time of signing
is the difference between them.
phrases.notes: "Them" means רבי שמעון and the רבנן.

steps.triggerLanguage: פֵּירֵי דְּמִשְּׁעַת כְּתִיבָה וְעַד שְׁעַת חֲתִימָה אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by naming a practical difference between רבי שמעון and the רבנן according to ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to ריש לקיש, רבי שמעון and the רבנן seemed to have nothing to argue about.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue about who owns the produce between the writing and the signing: the רבנן say it goes back to the wife from the signing, and רבי שמעון says from the writing.

steps.title: Elsewhere רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש hold the opposite views
steps.stepSummary: A different source records רבי יוחנן saying the husband loses the produce from the writing and ריש לקיש saying from the giving. That is the opposite of what the גמרא assumed earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we heard them say the opposite! As it was stated: From when does the court take the produce away from the husband? רבי יוחנן said: From the time of writing. ריש לקיש said: From the time of giving!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the earlier explanation by quoting another dispute where רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש seem to hold the reverse positions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 3, the גמרא said רבי יוחנן holds the husband keeps the produce until the גט is handed over, which is why the date does not matter to him. But this other source has רבי יוחנן saying the husband loses the produce already at the writing, and ריש לקיש saying only at the giving. Their positions look switched.

keyTerms.meaning: We heard them say the opposite
It was stated (introduces a recorded dispute between אמוראים)
The court takes the rights to the produce away from the husband
The time the גט is handed to the wife

phrases.english: But we heard them say the opposite!
phrases.notes: "Them" means רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. "The opposite" means the opposite of step 3.

phrases.english: As it was stated: From when does the court take away the produce?
phrases.notes: He means: from when does the husband lose his right to the produce of his wife's property?

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said: From the time of writing,
and ריש לקיש said: From the time of giving!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אִיפְּכָא שָׁמְעִינַן לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the claim from step 3 about רבי יוחנן's view on the produce and challenges it from an outside source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The positions given to רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about when the husband loses the produce (step 3)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A recorded dispute gives רבי יוחנן the 'writing' view and ריש לקיש the 'giving' view, which is the reverse of what the sugya assumed.

steps.title: Switch the names in the other dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the contradiction by reversing the names in the other source. ריש לקיש is the one who says 'from writing,' and רבי יוחנן says 'from giving.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers in one word: reverse the names in that other dispute so they match our sugya.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא keeps the explanation from this sugya and changes the other source instead. After the switch, רבי יוחנן holds the husband keeps the produce until the גט is given, as stated in step 3, and ריש לקיש holds it ends from the writing. The contradiction is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse it (switch the names of who said what)

steps.whatToRemember: According to the conclusion, רבי יוחנן dates the גט for the reason from steps 1-5 and holds the husband keeps the produce until the giving. ריש לקיש dates it because of the produce and holds the produce ends from the writing. רבי שמעון and the רבנן argue about the produce between the writing and the signing.
steps.confusionAlert: אֵיפוֹךְ here does not change our sugya. It changes the names in the other dispute that was just quoted.

phrases.english: Reverse it.
phrases.notes: Switch the names in the dispute just quoted: ריש לקיש says 'from writing,' and רבי יוחנן says 'from giving.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיפוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 8 by switching the names in the outside source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The other source seemed to show רבי יוחנן saying the produce ends at the writing, which contradicts step 3.
steps.terutzMaskana: The names in that source are reversed: רבי יוחנן says from the giving and ריש לקיש says from the writing, which fits this sugya.

steps.title: If an undated גט still works, what did the enactment accomplish?
steps.stepSummary: אביי points to the משנה that says an undated גט is invalid, but a child from a later marriage is still כשר. He asks what the חכמים gained by requiring a date at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: 'Three גיטין are invalid, but if she remarried, the child is כשר.' So what did the חכמים accomplish with their enactment?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a new set of questions about the rule that a גט must be dated. His first question challenges whether the rule does anything, since an undated גט still works after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An undated גט is one of the three 'invalid' גיטין, yet the divorce still takes effect and the child of a second marriage is fully כשר. If the גט works anyway, the date seems to add nothing. אביי wants to know what practical difference the enactment makes.

keyTerms.meaning: Three invalid bills of divorce. One of them is a גט with no date.
And if she remarried
The child is of fully acceptable lineage
A rule enacted by the חכמים

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
Three bills of divorce are invalid,
phrases.notes: He is quoting a משנה later in גיטין. One of the three is a גט without a date.

phrases.english: but if she married, the child is fine;
what did the Sages accomplish with their enactment?
phrases.notes: The enactment here is the rule, discussed earlier, that every גט must carry a date.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה הוֹעִילוּ חֲכָמִים בְּתַקָּנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new series of questions about the dating enactment, after the reasons for it were settled in earlier steps.
steps.kashyaTarget: The usefulness of the enactment requiring a date in a גט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an undated גט still takes effect and the child is כשר, the requirement seems to change nothing.

steps.title: The enactment means she may not remarry with it from the start
steps.stepSummary: The enactment does make a difference. With an undated גט, she is not allowed to remarry in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: It accomplished this: from the outset, she should not remarry.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer explains what the date requirement achieves. Even though an undated גט works after the fact, a woman holding one is not permitted to remarry in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The enactment works on the level of 'from the start' (לכתחילה), not 'after the fact' (בדיעבד). Because women will not be allowed to remarry with undated גיטין, people will make sure to date them. That is enough to give the rule real force.

keyTerms.meaning: They accomplished / it is effective
From the outset, before the fact
She should not remarry

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two levels. If she already remarried, the marriage stands and the child is כשר. The rule only stops her from remarrying with this גט in the first place.

phrases.english: It is effective in that she may not marry from the outset.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַהֲנוֹ דִּלְכַתְּחִילָּה לָא תִּינָּשֵׂא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes between 'from the start' and 'after the fact'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the undated גט works, the enactment has no effect.
steps.terutzMaskana: The enactment blocks remarriage from the start with an undated גט, even though it works after the fact.

steps.title: What if the husband cut off the date before giving it?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks about a גט that was properly dated when written, but the husband cut the date off before handing it to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he cut off its date and gave it to her, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks a follow-up. The גט was dated when it was written, but the husband removed the date before giving it. Is this treated like an undated גט, so she may not remarry with it from the start?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said an undated גט should not be used from the start. Here the גט was written correctly and the date was removed afterward. The question is whether that later removal makes it count as undated.

keyTerms.meaning: He cut it off
The date written in the גט
What is the law?

phrases.english: If he cut off its date,
and gave it to her, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּזְיֵיהּ לִזְמַן דִּידֵיהּ וְיַהֲבֵיהּ נִיהֲלַהּ מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 11's rule by testing an unusual case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a גט that was dated when written but had the date removed is treated as undated.

steps.title: We do not worry about a cheater
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that we do not worry about someone who deliberately cheats, so this גט is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We are not concerned about a deceiver.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers that the גט is fine to use. The rule was kept when the גט was written, and we do not make rules to guard against someone who deliberately tricks the system.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The enactment asks that a גט be written with a date, and this one was. Someone who cuts the date off afterward is acting like a cheater. The חכמים did not set their rule up to defend against that kind of rare, deliberate trick.

keyTerms.meaning: A cheater, a deceiver
We are not concerned

phrases.english: He said to him:
We are not concerned about a deceiver.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַמַּאי לָא חָיְישִׁינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The גט may be used, since we do not worry about a deceiver who removed a date that was properly written.

steps.title: What if the גט gives only a vague date?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks about a גט dated only by the שמיטה cycle, the year, the month or the week, with no exact day.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it has written in it only the seven-year cycle, the year, the month or the week, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks another follow-up. The גט has a date, but only a general one, such as which seven-year cycle, year, month or week. Is that good enough?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 established that a גט needs a date. Now the question is how exact that date must be. A general time span is written, but no specific day.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: the seven-year שמיטה cycle
Here: a week
Month

steps.confusionAlert: Here שבוע does not mean 'week'. It means a seven-year שמיטה cycle, and שבת is the word that means 'week'.

phrases.english: If written in it is the seven-year cycle, or the year,
or the month, or the week, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means only that general time span was written, with no exact day.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּתוּב בּוֹ שָׁבוּעַ שָׁנָה חֹדֶשׁ שַׁבָּת מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third question in the same series, about how exact the date must be.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a date that names only a general time span is enough to meet the enactment.

steps.title: A vague date is valid
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that such a גט is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers that a גט with only a general date is valid. Based on the question being asked, this means it may be used from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a general date counts as meeting the enactment. This sets up אביי's next challenge: if a vague date is enough, does the date still do its job?

keyTerms.meaning: Valid

phrases.english: He said to him: It is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ כָּשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גט dated only by cycle, year, month or week is valid.

steps.title: Then what does the enactment accomplish?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges the ruling. If a date that covers a whole seven-year span is enough, the date seems to protect against nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then what did the חכמים accomplish with their enactment?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's ruling. A date that covers years cannot pin down when the divorce happened, so how can it serve the purpose of the enactment?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps explained the date's purpose: knowing when the divorce took effect, for questions of adultery and of the produce. A date that only names a seven-year cycle leaves a huge gap. So it seems to defeat the whole point of dating the גט.

phrases.english: And what did the Sages accomplish with their enactment?
phrases.notes: Same words as in step 10, but now the worry is different: a vague date can't pin down when the divorce happened.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה הוֹעִילוּ חֲכָמִים בְּתַקָּנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's ruling that a vague date is valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The purpose of a date is to fix when the divorce took effect. A span of years cannot do that, so the enactment becomes pointless.

steps.title: It helps for the cycle before and the cycle after
steps.stepSummary: Even a vague date helps. It settles anything that happened in the seven-year cycle before it, or in the cycle after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is effective for the seven-year cycle before it and the seven-year cycle after it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers that a general date still does some good. It settles questions about events in the period before the stated span and in the period after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general date cannot settle what happened inside the stated span. But anything that happened in the earlier cycle clearly came before the divorce, and anything in the later cycle clearly came after it. That partial help is enough to count as meeting the enactment.

keyTerms.meaning: The one before it
The one after it

phrases.english: It helps for the seven-year cycle before it
and for the seven-year cycle after it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַהְנוֹ לְשָׁבוּעַ דְּקַמֵּיהּ וּלְשָׁבוּעַ דְּבָתְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A date must pin down the exact time, or else it is useless.
steps.terutzMaskana: A general date is useful because it settles events before and after its span.

steps.title: Even an exact day leaves a gap: morning or evening?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף supports his answer. Even a normal date naming one day does not tell us whether the divorce happened in the morning or the evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you do not say so, then on that day itself, do we know whether it was in the morning or in the evening?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף backs up his answer with a comparison. Even a fully exact date leaves some uncertainty within that day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal date names a day but not the hour. So if something happened on that same day, we still cannot tell whether it came before or after the divorce. This shows that no date gives perfect precision.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you do not say so
The day itself
From the morning
From the evening

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
phrases.notes: He means: if you don't accept that partial help is enough.

phrases.english: on the day itself, do we know
whether it was in the morning or in the evening?!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי יוֹמָא גּוּפֵיהּ מִי יָדְעִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 17 by showing that even an exact date leaves a gap.
steps.raayaObject: That a date which only partly settles the timing still counts
steps.raayaSupportSource: The plain logic that a normal day-date cannot separate morning from evening

steps.title: Just as a day helps for the days around it, a cycle helps for the cycles around it
steps.stepSummary: So even a regular date only settles the day before and the day after. In the same way, a cycle-date settles the cycle before and the cycle after.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it helps for the day before and the day after. Here too, it helps for the cycle before and the cycle after.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף finishes his comparison and applies it. A vague date works the same way as an exact one, just over a bigger span of time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal date really only settles events on the days before and after it. A cycle-date settles events in the cycles before and after it. The difference is only in how big the span is, not in how the date works, so both meet the enactment.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too
It is effective

steps.whatToRemember: An undated גט works after the fact, but she may not remarry with it from the start. We do not worry about a cheater who cuts off a date. Even a vague date is valid, because like any date it settles what happened before and after its span.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the date in a גט is meant to give useful help, not perfect precision. That is why a general date still satisfies the חכמים' enactment.

phrases.english: Rather, it helps for the day before it
and the day after it;
here too, it helps for the seven-year cycle before it
and the seven-year cycle after it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי אַהְנִי לְשָׁבוּעַ דְּקַמֵּיהּ וּלְשָׁבוּעַ דְּבָתְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the comparison from step 18 and applies it to the cycle-date.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A general date is valid. Like an exact date, it settles the periods before and after it, only over a larger span.

steps.title: רבינא begins a new question to רבא
steps.stepSummary: רבינא opens a question to רבא about a case where someone writes the גט. Only the first words of the case appear here.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רבא: If he writes the bill of divorce...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new question. רבינא starts describing a case to רבא about writing the גט, and the details come in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line starts a new topic after the discussion of the seven-year cycle date. The word כתביה, 'he wrote it', tells us the case is about the act of writing the גט. We have to wait for the rest of the case to know what רבינא is asking.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who asks the question here
The אמורא being asked
He wrote it (the גט)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not finished here. Don't try to work out the answer yet; the rest of the case comes in the next lines.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rava:
If he writes it
phrases.notes: 'It' means the גט. The rest of the case continues right after this word.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question after the conclusion about cycle-dates in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the law treats a particular case of writing the גט. The case is only beginning here.
